title: Montana motor-dealer data: who may see the customer records?
description: Learn why permission to use dealer data, the software contract and a safe supplier change need separate decisions.
learningSummary: A supplier may need warranty information without needing access to every customer record. Montana has specific rules for data held by qualifying new-motor-vehicle dealers. Start by identifying the business and the data, then separate permission to share from the contract that supplies the software.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, the new motor vehicle dealer identified through Montana’s statutory definitions; the word does not include every business selling equipment.
A business that connects systems so data can move between them.
The dealer’s express written permission for the specified data access or sharing.
Based on a qualifying reason under the law, rather than a decision made without stating such a reason.

sections.heading: Start with the business using the software
paragraphs: Imagine a manufacturer asking its Montana partner to connect its customer-management system to a new supplier portal. The system may contain warranty records, customer contacts and sales information. Signing a general brand agreement does not answer who may receive each part of that information.

Montana section 30-11-717 uses a particular meaning of dealer, linked to the new motor vehicle dealer definition in 61-4-201. An ordinary service franchise, standalone repair shop or used-only dealer has not been shown to qualify simply because it uses dealer software. The first document to prepare is a short explanation of which legal business fits which definition.

sections.heading: Permission needs its own document
paragraphs: For covered third-party access, the prescribed permission must be prior, express and written, in a document separate from other consent, contract or franchise writings. It must identify the sharing parties and contain the required details about what sharing is allowed and for how long. A broad paragraph inside the software subscription is not a substitute for checking those requirements.

Section 718 also restricts access, use, sharing and specified interference through technology or contracts, and addresses cyber ransom. List the actual manufacturer, software vendor, authorised integrator and other recipients: their legal roles can produce different duties.

sections.heading: Withdrawing access and ending a contract use different clocks
paragraphs: Under section 718, the prescribed consent can be revoked or amended on 30 days’ notice without cause, and immediately for cause. Sections 719–720 separately address vendor or integrator contract termination on their stated 90-day terms. These are different decisions; a long subscription term does not settle whether particular data permission continues.

The transition provisions also concern usable electronic data, return or deletion following the dealer’s written directions, recipient lists and audit access. An audit is a check of what happened to the data. Plan the successor’s access, export format and lawful retention before the old connection is switched off.

sections.heading: Worked example: warranty information versus a marketing feed
paragraphs: Fictional example: a foreign manufacturer needs warranty records from its Montana new-motor-vehicle dealer. It also wants the same connection to deliver the dealer’s entire customer list for marketing. The operations manager separates those requests instead of approving one unlimited feed.

Sections 717(9) and 719 distinguish required manufacturer data and specified purposes, including particular transactions, warranty or recall work, performance and other listed functions. The manager records each field and purpose, checks the required-data conditions and identifies any additional consent needed. Section 719 also permits the stated compliant push or submission alternative; direct entry into the dealer’s system is not the only possible method. Marketing data is not automatically required manufacturer data.

sections.heading: Prepare a practical access register
bullets: For each recipient, record its legal name, role, data fields, purpose and access method.
Attach the separate consent, permitted duration and instructions for changing or withdrawing it.
Keep the consent-notice date separate from any vendor-contract notice date.
Test an export to the replacement system; assign return/deletion instructions, recipient records and audit access.
Ask separately what other privacy, security and retention duties apply. The register is a planning tool, not approval of the transfer.

practicalOutput: A recipient-by-recipient data register with separate consent documents, notice dates and a tested vendor-transition checklist.
limitations: This covers the named Montana motor-dealer provisions and their referenced definition, not general franchise data or construction-equipment law.
Actual roles, purposes, statutory exceptions and other privacy/security or retention duties need their own review; no vendor or data transfer is approved.

title: Nebraska: choose the filing route before recruiting a partner
description: Understand the difference between a qualifying franchise notice and the separate seller-assisted marketing-plan process.
learningSummary: A business can qualify for an exemption and still have to notify Nebraska before specified recruitment activity. The seller must first establish which legal route applies to its actual offer. Preparing disclosure documents and obtaining a state filing acknowledgment are separate tasks, and neither proves that sales claims are accurate.

keyTerms.meaning: A rule that removes specified duties when all its conditions are met; it does not remove every law.
Seller-Assisted Marketing Plan: the category regulated by Nebraska’s Seller-Assisted Marketing Plan Act.
Franchise Disclosure Document: information supplied to a prospective franchise buyer, not government approval.
Money or another thing of value given as part of a commitment.

sections.heading: Why the campaign needs a legal decision first
paragraphs: A brand may prepare a website, book a Nebraska recruitment advertisement and arrange calls with prospective operators before anyone signs a contract. Nebraska’s relevant filing trigger can arise during that earlier activity. The selling business therefore needs a decision before the campaign, not only a check on signing day.

Section 59-1722 creates a conditional franchise exemption from the SAMP Act. The current statute incorporates specified federal provisions as they existed on January 1, 2026. Establishing the exemption means checking those incorporated conditions; using the word licence or holding a completed FDD does not establish compliance by itself.

sections.heading: What the qualifying franchise route requires
paragraphs: The statute requires notice and a $100 fee before the specified Nebraska-based advertising, offers or representations to Nebraska prospects. Some state prohibitions remain applicable despite the exemption. Describe where the advertisement is placed, who receives the offer and which entity is selling, so the reviewer can apply the actual trigger.

The notice identifies the seller, contact details, operating name and plan description. The regulator describes the qualifying franchise notice as a one-time filing without renewal, while distinguishing contact-only amendments from other changes. Keep that distinction when updating the company record: “one time” is not a reason to ignore every later change. Acknowledgment records a filing event; it does not approve the offering or verify statements about profit.

sections.heading: If the exemption is not established, investigate the other route
paragraphs: A covered nonexempt SAMP has a different process. Section 59-1724 provides for a prior disclosure filing and $100 fee, material-change filings and annual updates. A material change is a change important to the required information; it cannot simply be parked until the next sales cycle.

Section 59-1732 also addresses disclosure at the first specified in-person or written communication and at least 48 hours before the relevant contract or consideration. Those state rules do not shorten an independently applicable federal disclosure period. First determine which rules cover the transaction, then put each applicable clock on the calendar.

sections.heading: Worked example: a training business starts its campaign
paragraphs: Fictional example: a UK training network plans an advertisement in a Nebraska publication, followed by operator interviews. Its manager has a draft FDD and assumes the next step is accepting deposits. Instead, the manager lists the advertisement date, intended recipients, first communications and proposed commitments.

The reviewer establishes whether the actual offer satisfies the conditional franchise exemption. If it does, the company arranges the required prior notice and fee and keeps the acknowledgment. If it does not, the manager pauses the assumed franchise-notice route and obtains a decision on the nonexempt SAMP requirements. This planning sequence prevents the wrong form from becoming the basis for the campaign.

sections.heading: Create one filing decision sheet
bullets: Name the selling entity, Nebraska prospects and relevant advertising or communication locations.
Record the exemption conditions, evidence and responsible reviewer; mark unresolved facts explicitly.
Attach the applicable form, payment, submission and acknowledgment before covered activity.
Calendar federal disclosure separately from any applicable state disclosure, amendment or annual task.
List relationship, industry and local operating questions that this filing decision does not answer.

practicalOutput: A dated Nebraska filing-route decision sheet linked to the recruitment calendar and retained notice or disclosure-filing evidence.
limitations: This explains the stated Nebraska filing and disclosure branches, not a complete state franchise or operating-law survey.
Federal disclosure and separate state sales, relationship, sector and local duties still depend on the actual parties, places and activities.

title: Nebraska earnings claims: explain where the numbers came from
description: Learn why a possible sales calculation is different from evidence supporting an income claim to a prospective buyer.
learningSummary: A spreadsheet can show how a business might make money without showing that purchasers have actually achieved those results. Nebraska’s stated SAMP earnings rule requires more than attractive arithmetic. First decide whether that particular rule applies, then separate internal planning assumptions from claims made to a prospective buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: A statement about income or earning potential made to help sell the opportunity.
Evidence that supports a claim, rather than a calculation showing it is possible.
The identified purchasers whose records are used to support the representation.
A covered seller-assisted marketing plan for which the relevant exemption has not been established.

sections.heading: Identify the offer before applying the claims rule
paragraphs: Section 59-1729 addresses earning-potential representations in covered seller-assisted marketing plans. Read it with the franchise exemption and other exclusions. This guide does not say that every SAMP marketing restriction survives for every qualifying exempt franchise.

That distinction matters to the seller preparing a pitch. The business should document its legal route rather than asking the marketing team to guess whether a franchise label removes the rule. Any applicable federal financial-performance requirements remain a separate question.

sections.heading: A multiplication is a scenario, not proof
paragraphs: The statute expressly says that multiplying sales by profit per sale is insufficient substantiation. Its required information includes the seller’s selling history, the number and percentage of purchasers forming the representation’s basis, and purchasers known to attain the stated results.

The number and percentage tell the buyer how much of the purchaser population supports the claim. For example, a result drawn from a small selected group cannot be understood without knowing who was included, who was left out and how the results were measured. Keep the underlying records so a reviewer can follow the calculation back to actual experience. This is different from choosing inputs that produce a desirable answer.

sections.heading: Worked example: the cleaning-account package
paragraphs: Fictional example: a seller models 20 cleaning accounts at $200 profit per account each month. The total is $4,000 per month. That calculation is mathematically correct if its assumptions hold, but it does not establish that purchasers obtained 20 accounts, kept them, or earned the assumed profit.

The expansion manager asks for the actual purchaser group, the period covered, the number and percentage represented and records of attained results. The manager also investigates what the number means: does it include travel, staff costs, account loss and the owner’s time? These questions help distinguish the advertised result from an internal management model; they do not themselves satisfy every statutory disclosure requirement.

If the seller cannot support the proposed representation, labelling the model “illustrative” does not supply the missing evidence. The team should obtain a decision on what, if anything, may be communicated rather than converting assumptions into a prospect-facing promise.

sections.heading: Control the material actually given to the purchaser
paragraphs: The rule addresses prescribed supporting data and disclosure to the purchaser. Decide when and how that data must be left with the purchaser under the applicable provision. A file kept only by the sales director may not answer the delivery duty.

Also check the applicable seller-identification requirements for nonexempt SAMP advertising. Slides, scripts, emails and calculators can communicate the same income message in different formats. Reviewing the whole set helps prevent a carefully limited written statement from becoming an unqualified oral sales claim.

sections.heading: Make a claim-by-claim evidence file
bullets: Write the exact proposed statement, intended audience and sales channel.
State the applicable exemption or nonexempt route and the reviewer’s reasoning.
Label every model with its period, place, currency and assumptions.
Identify the purchaser group, source records, exclusions, number and percentage, and known attainment evidence.
Record the required purchaser disclosure/delivery step and who must approve each sales-material version.

practicalOutput: A register pairing each proposed earnings statement with its purchaser records, calculation, applicable legal route and delivery instructions.
limitations: This is the stated Nebraska nonexempt SAMP claims branch, not a determination that every franchise is subject to it.
Federal financial-performance disclosure and other state sales, relationship, sector and local requirements remain independent; an internal model is not proof of a buyer’s future results.

title: Nebraska relationship law: why the business location and sales matter
description: Work through the separate tests that can govern an ongoing franchise relationship, even after a sales notice is filed.
learningSummary: A notice filed before selling an opportunity answers a different question from the rules governing an established business relationship. Nebraska’s Franchise Practices Act has its own definition and combined application tests. The supplier and operator need the location, payment, sales and contract facts before relying on its renewal or termination rules.

keyTerms.meaning: The business granting the relevant branded business rights.
The operator receiving those rights under the arrangement.
A legally sufficient reason under the relevant statute; it is not whatever reason the contract happens to list.
Allowing an agreement to end instead of continuing it for another term.

sections.heading: A filed sales notice does not decide the relationship question
paragraphs: The SAMP notice concerns the sales-law route. The Franchise Practices Act separately asks whether the arrangement fits its own definition and application criteria. Do not import the federal franchise definition or treat a filed notice as a decision about these ongoing protections.

The statutory definition includes specific nonalcoholic-beverage wording and excludes petroleum arrangements. It also defines franchise fee and good cause. Record the actual rights and payments rather than relying on what the parties call the agreement.

sections.heading: Apply all three statutory criteria
paragraphs: Section 87-403 requires the stated Nebraska place of business, gross sales of covered products or services between the parties exceeding $35,000 in the 12 months immediately before the lawsuit is filed, and more than 20 percent of the franchisee’s gross sales intended to be or derived from the franchise. The criteria are cumulative: meeting one does not replace the others.

The place-of-business definition concerns a fixed place where the operator displays and sells goods or offers and sells the franchisor’s services. It expressly excludes an office, warehouse, storage place, residence or vehicle. An address in Nebraska is therefore not enough by itself. The sales amounts are tests for this law, not a general minimum business size for entering the state.

sections.heading: Worked example: a travelling technical-service business
paragraphs: Fictional example: a Dutch supplier appoints an operator that keeps an office and sends technicians to customers. The operator expects most of its income to come from the brand. That expectation may be relevant to one sales-allocation question, but it does not establish a qualifying place of business or the required sales between the parties.

The team maps where customers actually obtain services, what happens at each location, the branded rights and the fee structure. Finance separately records the relevant 12-month sales between the parties and the operator’s intended or actual franchise-related share of gross sales. The result is a factual file for applying all tests, not an assumption that an office-based business is either protected or excluded in every case.

sections.heading: Then identify the particular action and exception
paragraphs: Section 87-404 generally combines good cause with written reasons at least 60 days in advance. It also has an abandonment branch and specified grounds with immediate-notice treatment. Its noncompetition provisions have separate scope. Do not send a termination letter merely because a generic calendar allows 60 days.

Section 87-404(1) also preserves a contract provision making the franchise nonrenewable, or renewable only if stated reasonable conditions are met. Good-cause language is not a promise of indefinite renewal. Review the actual contract, action, reasons and statutory branch together.

sections.heading: Prepare the relationship decision file
bullets: Map actual locations and how goods or services reach customers.
Attach brand rights, payment terms and facts about the parties’ shared commercial interests.
Preserve the specified 12-month sales between the parties and the operator’s franchise-sales allocation.
Keep contract term, renewal conditions, alleged defaults and contemporaneous records together.
Before termination, nonrenewal or enforcement, record the applicable statutory branch and actual notice requirements.

practicalOutput: A location-and-sales fact file plus a separate decision on the proposed renewal, termination or other relationship action.
limitations: This explains the named Franchise Practices Act provisions, not a complete Nebraska sales, relationship or operating-law survey.
Actual definitions, cumulative criteria, contract terms and exceptions require application to the facts; federal, sector and local duties remain separate.

title: Nevada farm-equipment dealers: plan changes and exit before signing
description: Understand why equipment inventory and dependence on a supplier can create duties beyond the brand agreement.
learningSummary: A company selling farm machines through a Nevada dealer may have to plan for more than the contract’s end date. The defined farm-equipment dealer law addresses reasons for major changes, termination, notice and inventory repurchase. Establish whether that law covers the arrangement before applying any of its numbers.

keyTerms.meaning: The supplier–dealer arrangement to be tested against the statute’s actual definition.
A sufficient reason under the relevant law, requiring more than pointing to a broad contractual right.
An opportunity to correct a stated deficiency.
A supplier buying back qualifying property under applicable conditions; not reimbursement of every investment.

sections.heading: Why this is an equipment question
paragraphs: Nevada NRS 597.112–597.118 concerns defined farm-equipment dealer relationships. Its tests include retail inventory rights, a distribution-system role and substantial dependence on a supplier. Inventory means the defined farm equipment, attachments or repair parts. A maintenance-service brand or software licence does not fit merely because the parties use the word dealer.

The supplier and proposed operator should list the actual machines, parts, distribution rights and sources of revenue. That list helps the reviewer apply the statutory definition instead of copying a rule from another industry.

sections.heading: Termination and nonrenewal have a particular procedure
paragraphs: Section 597.1143 addresses good cause and generally requires 180 days’ written reasons before termination or nonrenewal, with 60 days to correct specified deficiencies. Listed grounds receive different treatment, and market-share failures have an assistance condition. The general periods therefore cannot be applied without checking the reason for action.

A contractual end date does not complete the analysis. Keep the alleged deficiency, performance evidence, support offered and proposed corrective steps together. They help explain whether the applicable statutory branch has been followed; simply waiting out a notice period cannot establish good cause.

sections.heading: A major amendment is not automatically governed by the same clock
paragraphs: Section 597.1143(1) also requires good cause for a substantial change of a covered agreement’s terms. Section 597.115(4) addresses termination, nonrenewal and those changes because of natural disaster, labour dispute or similar circumstances beyond the dealer’s control. Section 597.118 prohibits waiver or modification of the statutory rights, obligations and liabilities.

The 180-day notice and 60-day correction provisions in subsections (2)–(3) concern termination and nonrenewal. They do not establish a universal 180-day notice for every amendment. Compare the old and proposed terms and explain why the supplier wants the change.

sections.heading: Worked example: a farm-machine network changes direction
paragraphs: Fictional example: a European manufacturer appoints a Nevada dealer to sell agricultural machines, stock parts and perform branded servicing. Later, the manufacturer considers changing the agreement substantially or ending it after weak sales. The manager first checks whether the arrangement falls within the farm-equipment definitions.

The team then separates the proposed action from its reason. A substantial amendment raises the good-cause question; a termination or nonrenewal also requires the correct notice and correction analysis. If the problem is market share, the assistance condition needs attention. If a natural disaster affected performance, the separate uncontrollable-circumstances provision must be examined. The same notice template cannot answer every branch.

sections.heading: Keep the possible buyback separate from the accounting balance
paragraphs: The chapter has repurchase rules and exclusions based on inventory condition, age and other facts, including specified supplier-required systems and tools. Retain purchase and requirement records now. Neither the gross inventory total nor the amount spent on technology proves what must be bought back.

sections.heading: Make the equipment relationship file usable
bullets: List covered equipment, parts, supplier rights and the basis for dealer-law coverage.
Retain invoices, purchase dates, condition and current catalogue information.
Identify required systems/tools, warranty responsibilities and payments.
Keep proposed term changes, reasons, performance notices, assistance and correction evidence.
Assign separate reviews for franchise sales and other industry or local duties.

practicalOutput: A farm-equipment coverage decision, a proposed-action comparison and an item-by-item inventory/required-systems file.
limitations: The cited chapter concerns defined farm-equipment dealer arrangements, not all Nevada franchises or service businesses.
Coverage, good cause, notice exceptions and repurchase eligibility require actual facts; federal disclosure and other state, sector and local duties are separate.

title: New Hampshire recruitment plans: follow the money through every level
description: Learn how to examine successive recruitment rights without assuming a master-operator title decides the legal result.
learningSummary: A regional partner may recruit operators and also provide valuable training and support. New Hampshire separately prohibits a defined chain-distributor sales device. To understand the distinction, trace what each participant must pay, what recruiting rights they receive and how money moves through the network.

keyTerms.meaning: The payment or investment condition to examine under this statutory definition.
A participant’s right to bring additional participants into the arrangement for economic gain.
A commercial role that may include recruitment and support; the title does not decide the statutory test.
The rules showing who earns money, from which activity and from whose payment.

sections.heading: Start with the actual offer, not its name
paragraphs: A supplier might call its partner a master franchisee, regional licensee or representative. Those words can describe business responsibilities, but they do not establish whether the sales arrangement meets RSA 358-B. The reviewed law focuses on a particular combination of required investment and successive recruiting rights.

The test concerns participants who make an investment and receive rights to recruit others for economic gain, with those further participants also investing and receiving recruiting rights. Read the complete arrangement through each level. A recruitment fee alone, or genuine master-operator duties alone, does not establish every element.

sections.heading: Why a territory limit does not answer the question
paragraphs: The law expressly says that limiting the number of participants or adding eligibility conditions does not itself change the identity of the defined scheme. A cap can affect the commercial scale without resolving the statutory structure.

Where the prohibited device is established, the chapter prohibits promotion, offering or granting participation. The company therefore needs the review before recruitment activity, rather than waiting to see whether the network becomes large or profitable. This page does not conclude that every multi-level business or master franchise is unlawful.

sections.heading: Separate customers from participants in the accounts
paragraphs: A useful management exercise is to draw two money flows: revenue from delivering services to customers, and payments connected with joining or recruiting into the network. Identify each recipient and the conditions for earning each amount. This is a planning method for exposing the facts, not an independent legal safe harbour.

Also describe the support actually delivered. Training, site visits and quality checks have costs and responsible people. An unsupported statement that a payment buys “support” does not show what the parties do. Conversely, documenting real support does not replace applying the complete statutory test.

sections.heading: Worked example: a technical-services network
paragraphs: Fictional example: a foreign brand proposes a regional partner paid when new operators join. Each operator may then buy rights to recruit further operators. The board initially focuses on the fact that only ten regional territories will be sold.

The expansion manager instead draws the arrangement across several levels. For each participant, the manager records required payments, recruiting rights and the source of compensation. A separate column records customer service revenue and actual training or field-support duties. The board can now ask whether the economic arrangement meets every element of the defined chain-distributor device, rather than treating the territory cap as an exemption.

If the review identifies unresolved facts, the next step is to clarify the contracts and payment plan before promoting participation. The fictional example demonstrates the investigation; it does not determine whether any particular arrangement is prohibited.

sections.heading: Prepare a compensation and delivery map
bullets: List every required upfront or continuing payment and its recipient.
Show which participants receive recruiting rights and whether those rights pass to further participants.
Separate customer-contract income from participant-recruitment payments.
Cost and assign the promised training, field support and quality responsibilities.
Get a decision on the full statutory structure before offers, without relying on a territory cap.

practicalOutput: A diagram of participant payments and successive recruiting rights, supported by the actual contracts and a costed support plan.
limitations: RSA 358-B is the specific statutory branch reviewed here; master-operator duties or a recruitment fee alone do not establish all elements.
Federal franchise disclosure, New Hampshire consumer protection, industry dealer rules and other operating duties need separate review. Unresearched requirements are not treated as absent.

title: New Hampshire equipment dealers: check the sales and service rights
description: Understand why an industrial-equipment or authorised-service partner may need a dealer-law review even without a car showroom.
learningSummary: A company may think it is licensing a maintenance service while also giving the operator equipment-sales and warranty rights. Those rights can make an industry dealer statute relevant. New Hampshire’s chapter title is only a starting point: examine the defined products, parties and service arrangements before choosing the contract.

keyTerms.meaning: Service the supplier or manufacturer has permitted the business to provide under the arrangement.
Whether the actual business falls within the people, products and agreements covered by the statute.
A legally sufficient reason for the stated action under the applicable provision.
A formal route to challenge an action where the applicable law provides one.

sections.heading: Why an equipment business should read beyond the title
paragraphs: RSA 357-C includes specified farm, utility, forestry, industrial, construction, yard and garden equipment within its defined framework. A European business cannot decide that the chapter is irrelevant simply because it does not sell ordinary passenger cars.

Equally, the equipment list does not establish that every machine-service arrangement is covered. The definitions describe particular sellers, rights and arrangements, including service rights and exceptions. There is a specified single-line equipment-dealer exception whose actual conditions need review. Record the inventory and supplier relationship before applying the statute.

sections.heading: Describe what the operator is allowed to do
paragraphs: The chief operating officer should separate equipment sales, distribution, authorised servicing and warranty work. Identify the company granting each right, the products involved and the brand used with customers. Continuing dependence on parts or supply also belongs in the factual description.

A service-only agreement involving fleet, government or rental vehicles has express treatment in the definitions. Those customer and use facts matter; a repair business serving one kind of customer should not copy a conclusion about a different arrangement. This guide explains what to investigate, rather than deciding that a proposed operator meets every test.

sections.heading: Worked example: adding a machine line to a service business
paragraphs: Fictional example: a European industrial-maintenance brand plans a New Hampshire operator. Its original budget assumes technicians selling their labour. The revised agreement also permits equipment sales and manufacturer-authorised warranty work on one machine line.

The expansion manager makes a table with one row for each activity: machine sales, ordinary maintenance, warranty work and parts supply. Each row identifies the relevant entity, customer type, product use and continuing supplier rights. The reviewer then tests those facts against RSA 357-C, including any relevant single-line or service-only provision.

This exercise has a commercial benefit even before the legal result is known. The manager can see that warranty training, spare-parts commitments and continuing supplier support may cost more than the original labour-only plan allowed. Those are planning questions, not additional duties asserted by this page.

sections.heading: Keep the relationship process available before a dispute
paragraphs: The chapter contains good-faith, good-cause, notice and protest provisions for covered relationships. Good faith concerns the standard of conduct required by the applicable provision; it is not established merely because an agreement contains that phrase.

The complete RSA 357-C:7 route must be reviewed for the particular event. This page supplies neither a universal notice period nor a decision about compensation. Before changing or ending an arrangement, preserve the current agreement, proposed action, reasons and relevant communications so the correct process can be examined.

sections.heading: Prepare the product-and-rights worksheet
bullets: Describe each product and component, its use and who supplies it.
List sales, distribution, service and warranty rights separately by legal entity.
Record supplier concentration and facts relevant to any single-line exception.
Identify fleet, government or rental customers and the actual service limitations.
Attach proposed changes or exit reasons and assign review of the complete applicable process.

practicalOutput: A worksheet connecting actual equipment, customer uses and sales/service rights to a specific dealer-law review.
limitations: This is a review of the named New Hampshire equipment/dealer branch, not a complete franchise or operating-law survey.
Actual definitions, exceptions and the relevant RSA 357-C:7 process must be applied separately; no general notice period, compensation entitlement or legal clearance is established.

title: New Jersey B2B partners: why an office or warehouse can matter
description: Learn which business-location and relationship facts to investigate before assuming a distributor falls outside franchise protections.
learningSummary: A partner selling to industrial customers may work from an office or warehouse rather than a shop. New Jersey’s identified enacted amendment shows why that difference cannot end the franchise-law inquiry. This guide teaches the relevant factual questions while preserving the limit that the complete current codification was unavailable during review.

keyTerms.meaning: Business to business: sales to other businesses rather than directly to consumers.
The organised published version of a law, incorporating amendments.
The shared financial or economic interest in the relationship, requiring examination of the actual dependence and investment facts.
Facts asserted in a court case at a stage when the court has not necessarily found them to be true.

sections.heading: Look at how the business actually reaches customers
paragraphs: The identified enacted amendment to New Jersey’s Franchise Practices Act expressly addresses businesses that do not make a majority of sales directly to consumers. Its place-of-business wording includes qualifying offices or warehouses from which personnel visit or call customers, or goods are delivered.

That wording makes the real operation worth investigating. It does not mean every warehouse qualifies. Record what happens at the location, what is sold, how customers are contacted and whether most sales are directly to consumers or business buyers. A note saying “no retail outlet” leaves those questions unanswered.

sections.heading: A location is only part of the relationship analysis
paragraphs: The Act’s definition also addresses a written arrangement, licensed brand characteristics and a community of interest. The reviewer needs the agreement and the parties’ actual course of dealing: how they have conducted the business, not just the title printed on the contract.

A cited 2025 federal district-court opinion explains why calling an arrangement distribution does not resolve those factual questions. The opinion was testing pleaded allegations, not making final factual findings. Its lesson here is to gather the relevant evidence; it is not a final ruling that every distributor is a franchisee.

sections.heading: Worked example: industrial customer visits from an office
paragraphs: Fictional example: a Dutch equipment-support supplier appoints a New Jersey operator. Staff telephone industrial customers from an office and visit customer premises. Equipment is delivered from a warehouse. Management initially assumes the absence of a consumer shop removes the relationship-law question.

The expansion lead instead describes the office and delivery functions, the buyer mix, the customer-facing brand and the written rights. Finance identifies investments useful mainly within this particular relationship. The team also records the relevant sales/application criteria for the reviewer, rather than deciding coverage from location alone.

If the supplier later wants to withdraw branded rights, the same factual file supports review before action. The example does not establish that the operator qualifies, or specify a lawful termination period. It shows why preparing the evidence early is more useful than trying to reconstruct the business after a dispute.

sections.heading: Keep the source limitation visible
paragraphs: The legislature’s webpage for the current codified law returned an error during the recorded review. The enacted amendment and the identified primary judicial opinion were read, but they do not certify the complete 2026 Act. A proposal to grant, change or withdraw rights still needs the applicable current statutory text and relevant industry rules.
Questions about registration, notice, disclosure and advertising remain separate research questions. The limited sources supporting this page are not evidence that those requirements are absent.

sections.heading: Prepare the reviewer’s factual file
bullets: Map products/services, customer contact and delivery locations.
Show the proportion and nature of consumer versus business sales.
Attach written brand rights and a description of actual dealings.
Identify investment tied mainly to this relationship and the relevant sales facts.
Assign retrieval of the current full law before relying on an eligibility or relationship-action conclusion.

practicalOutput: A B2B location-and-relationship factsheet that identifies the missing current-codification review as an open task.
limitations: The complete current New Jersey codification was not retrieved; this page is limited to the identified enacted amendment and primary judicial explanation.
No definitive 2026 eligibility, filing or termination conclusion is made. The judicial discussion of allegations is not a final factual finding about the reader’s arrangement.

title: New Mexico termination rules: check whether the document became law
description: Use the official status of the failed 2026 proposal to avoid importing a proposed notice period into a live contract.
learningSummary: An official-looking bill can describe detailed protections without creating a current duty. New Mexico’s 2026 SB 115 is an example: the official record says the proposal died. Before a supplier relies on a dealer-termination template, it must distinguish proposed text from the currently enacted rules.

keyTerms.meaning: A proposal submitted to the legislature; publication alone does not make it law.
The process by which a proposal becomes law.
The organised published statutory text to check for the rules currently applicable.
An analysis of a proposal, including its possible effects; it is not itself enacted legislation.

sections.heading: Why this source distinction affects a real business decision
paragraphs: A supplier ending a dealer arrangement needs to know which rules govern the actual products, parties and agreement. A proposed notice period can look particularly convincing because it is precise. Precision in a draft is not evidence that the legislature adopted it.

New Mexico’s official 2026 SB 115 status page records “Died (API)”. Here API records action postponed indefinitely. The introduced text and its analysis discussed expanded equipment definitions and termination protections, but those changes did not become law through this bill.

sections.heading: A proposed effective date is conditional
paragraphs: A legislative analysis may explain when a measure would take effect if enacted. That date cannot establish that enactment occurred. The 2026 Fiscal Impact Report also says similar proposals in 2023 and 2025 were not enacted.

Keep four documents conceptually separate: the introduced bill, analysis of the bill, any enacted chapter and the current codified statute. They can answer different questions. This guide verifies the failed proposal’s status; it does not replace retrieval of the current Franchise Termination Act.

sections.heading: Worked example: a machinery supplier updates its template
paragraphs: Fictional example: a European machinery business finds the 2026 proposal while preparing a notice to its New Mexico dealer. A manager copies the proposed supplier-notice period into a standard U.S. template and treats that number as the final check before sending it.

The colleague reviewing the file checks the session, version and official final status. Because the bill died, the proposed period cannot justify the notice. The colleague removes the unsupported assumption from the decision process and asks for the currently enacted statute, its equipment/dealer definitions, the signed agreement and any independently applicable federal rules.

That correction does not establish a shorter period or permission to terminate immediately. It changes the question from “Have we waited the number in the bill?” to “Which enacted provisions actually govern this relationship and this action?” The notice remains subject to that unresolved review.

sections.heading: Keep a source-status record alongside the contract
bullets: Save the exact bill number, session, version and official final status.
Mark introduced text and legislative analysis as proposal material.
Obtain the current enacted/codified provisions before choosing a notice procedure.
Describe the actual equipment, dealer rights, parties and intended relationship action.
Check the contract and independently applicable federal or industry rules.
Leave franchise sales, disclosure and local operating questions open until they have their own evidence.

practicalOutput: A short bill-status record attached to a task for obtaining the applicable enacted relationship rules before any notice is issued.
limitations: Current statutory coverage remains unresolved here; the verified conclusion concerns the cited proposal’s non-enactment.
No conclusion is made that franchise filings or existing dealer protections are absent, and no termination is approved.

title: New York franchises: keep the meeting, filing and renewal clocks separate
description: Understand how classification, disclosure, annual renewal, advertising and material changes create different management tasks.
learningSummary: A New York franchise sale may involve duties well before signature, and the company’s annual renewal process does not replace them. First establish whether the actual arrangement and state connections bring it within the relevant rules. Then keep meetings, documents, money, advertising and registration status on separate but connected calendars.

keyTerms.meaning: Franchise Disclosure Document: information for a prospective buyer, not approval of the business.
The company’s accounting year, which need not end on December 31.
An important change requiring review under the applicable prospectus amendment rule.
A legally defined working-day count; it must not be silently substituted for a calendar-day count.
Giving up a right; statutes can restrict attempts to require a buyer to give up statutory protections.
Money or another thing of value given in connection with the relevant commitment.

sections.heading: New York’s definition has alternative branches
paragraphs: The Attorney General says covered offerings must be registered before franchises are offered or sold in or from New York unless an exemption applies. General Business Law (GBL) 681(3) has two alternative franchise branches: a substantially prescribed marketing plan plus a required direct or indirect fee, or substantial association with the designated commercial symbol plus that fee. Both the plan and symbol elements are not required in every arrangement.

Section 681 also addresses fee exclusions, area/subfranchise roles, uninterrupted renewals and state connections. Part 200.1 adds fee and advice/training meanings. List the actual seller, rights, payments, support, offers, acceptances and operating locations before applying a branch or exemption. This guide does not classify a particular transaction.

sections.heading: Disclosure can be due before the expected signing date
paragraphs: GBL 683(8) requires the offering prospectus—the seller’s required disclosure information—and proposed agreements at the earliest of the first personal meeting, at least ten business days before a binding franchise or other agreement, or at least ten days before receipt of consideration. It defines the covered first face-to-face meeting by its purpose of discussing a sale or possible franchise sale. Record the meeting’s purpose as well as its date.

The currently linked Attorney General addendum, revised April 2, 2024, instead uses ten-business-day wording alongside execution or related payment. Preserve that literal source difference. The federal 14-calendar-day requirement is independent: it does not justify ignoring the state’s earlier meeting or payment trigger. Do not silently change the statute’s ten-day payment language into ten business days.

sections.heading: Annual renewal follows the accounting calendar
paragraphs: The Attorney General’s guide directs annual renewal submissions within 120 days after the franchisor’s fiscal year end. It distinguishes a timely pending renewal from expired registration. If registration expires, the guide says there can be no covered offers or sales within or from New York until renewal is submitted and accepted for filing.

The renewal package includes an updated FDD, marked changes, accountant consent, franchise-sales information, prices, credit terms and audited financial statements. Finance and sales teams must both contribute. An internal preparation schedule is a useful business control; it does not change the legal deadline.

sections.heading: New information and new advertising need their own checks
paragraphs: Part 200.5 requires prompt notification by an application to amend for material prospectus changes. Its examples include fees, specified significant adverse business/obligation/agreement/product or model changes and stated financial information. Keep a change register independently of the annual renewal.

The agency guide also calls for two copies of franchise advertising through FRED at least seven days before intended use. FRED is the franchise filing system of the North American Securities Administrators Association (NASAA). Annual renewal does not complete that separate campaign task; current guidance controls the submission channel.

sections.heading: Worked example: the recruitment season overlaps year end
paragraphs: Fictional example: a UK training network plans personal sales meetings during its busiest recruitment period, shortly after fiscal year end. The finance director gathers renewal information while the expansion director records the actual first meeting, document-delivery, signature and payment dates. Neither assumes that preparing the annual filing has authorised the meetings.

Marketing separately records the advertisement’s intended use and submission. If fees or another material prospectus fact changes, the team opens an amendment task instead of waiting for next year. If registration lapses, it records the affected activities and conditions for resuming them. One shared calendar can contain all these tasks, but one completed task cannot stand in for the others.

sections.heading: Review the whole signing package
paragraphs: GBL 687(4)–(5) addresses waiver of statutory compliance and required release, assignment, novation, waiver or estoppel relieving statutory duty or liability. These terms concern ways to give up, replace, transfer or prevent assertion of rights. The actual wording and signing context matter; the provisions do not decide every later negotiated settlement.

The addendum addresses preserved rights in renewal/transfer and choice clauses, and limits the stated claim-waiver or reliance-disclaimer effects of commencement questionnaires/acknowledgments. Compare all side documents, not only the main agreement.

sections.heading: Prepare the management calendar and document pack
bullets: Record fiscal year end, renewal dates, accountable owners and financial/sales inputs.
Keep registered and proposed FDD/agreement versions, marked changes and amendment decisions.
Log actual meetings, deliveries, signatures and consideration, with each applicable timing rule.
Retain advertising versions, two-copy submissions and intended-use dates.
Review questionnaires, acknowledgments and other side papers with the applicable addendum.

practicalOutput: A linked renewal, sales-event, amendment and advertising calendar supported by the actual document versions and signing package.
limitations: The specific state and federal duties discussed do not complete tax, employment, permits, industry or address-dependent review.
Actual offer locations, entities, model, exemptions and dates require review. The statute/addendum wording difference is preserved, not resolved by silently substituting one clock.

title: New York franchise advertisements: plan the seven-day submission
description: Learn what to record before a recruitment advertisement is used and why the exact version matters.
learningSummary: A recruitment advertisement can reach a prospective operator before the sales team has a conversation. New York’s Attorney General guide therefore gives advertising its own submission timetable. The practical task is to identify what will actually be published, submit the required material and control later edits.

keyTerms.meaning: Material used in offering or selling franchises; whether a particular communication qualifies requires review.
North American Securities Administrators Association.
The franchise filing system identified by the agency for this submission.
Keeping a dated copy of each edition so the submitted advertisement can be compared with the one actually used.

sections.heading: The agency’s stated timing rule
paragraphs: The current Attorney General guide requires two copies of advertising used in offering or selling franchises, submitted through NASAA FRED at least seven days before intended use. Identify the actual material, channel, sponsor and planned first-use date before organising that submission.

This is a submission requirement, not a statement that filing an advertisement certifies its contents. Nor does this guide automatically decide whether every website page, message or conversation is a franchise advertisement. The company should obtain a decision for the actual communication instead of assuming that a particular format removes the question.

sections.heading: Why marketing and sales need the same record
paragraphs: The person submitting the material may work from a PDF, while an agency controls a website and sales staff circulate slides. Without an exact record, management may be unable to show that the material scheduled for use is the version reviewed and submitted.

A practical campaign record can contain the document or screenshot, the planned audience, the editor and the intended first use. This record is a management method for keeping track of the stated duty. It does not create a new legal filing category or establish an exemption.

sections.heading: Worked example: a landing page changes after submission
paragraphs: Fictional example: a French training brand prepares a New York recruitment campaign. Its filing team retains the advertisement and submission receipt. The external marketing agency later revises the landing page to make the opportunity more appealing.

The operations manager compares the revised live-page draft with the retained submitted version. If they differ, the manager asks whether the change requires further review or filing before use; the manager does not assume that review of an earlier PDF covers the new page. The intended publication date remains visible while that question is resolved.

The same comparison identifies any changed financial statement in the advertisement. The manager asks who supplied its evidence and whether the final wording still matches it. This example is fictional and does not establish the permissibility of a particular earnings claim or advertisement.

Keeping the evidence together also makes a delay easier to manage. Marketing can change a publication schedule deliberately rather than discovering at launch that the record does not support the material currently scheduled. That is an operational benefit, not a promise that the regulator will approve a campaign.

sections.heading: Use a short publication checklist
bullets: Give the campaign a reference and retain the exact document or screenshot version.
Record the audience, New York connections, sponsor and planned first-use date.
Keep the two submitted copies, submission date and receipt together.
Identify the responsible editor and evidence behind any earnings statement.
Compare the scheduled final material with the submitted version; resolve changes before use.
Check registration, any claimed exemption and buyer disclosure separately. An advertising submission does not complete them.

practicalOutput: A campaign record containing the precise advertisement, two-copy submission evidence, intended-use date and final-version comparison.
limitations: This teaches the advertising submission rule described by the agency, not an automatic classification of every communication.
Registration, exemptions and buyer disclosure are distinct; tax, employment and operating-permit requirements also remain outside this guide. Actual parties, offer locations and dates need review.

title: New York pay budgets: choose the location, industry and year first
description: Use the dated 2026 wage posters correctly before turning an hourly minimum into a cleaning or building-service budget.
learningSummary: The same employer can face different minimum-pay figures at different New York worksites. Industry and worker category also matter, so a cleaning label alone does not select the correct rule. Begin with the actual location and pay period, then add the other required pay and employer costs separately.

keyTerms.meaning: New York State Department of Labor, the agency publishing the cited wage information.
The set of pay rules applicable to a particular industry or type of work.
Treating a permitted amount of tips toward an employer’s wage obligation where the applicable rules allow it.
A separate pay issue flagged by the relevant rules concerning the span of a working day.
The agency’s stated mechanism affecting a scheduled rate increase; an announcement about it is distinct from a proposed law.

sections.heading: Use the worksite and the date, not just the company address
paragraphs: The cited miscellaneous-industry and building-service posters cover January 1 through December 31, 2026. They show $17 per hour in New York City, Long Island and Westchester County, and $16 in the rest of the state. An Albany worksite and a Westchester worksite therefore need different regional entries even if one employer supplies both.

Keep the dated poster with the payroll calculation. A table found later on an agency overview may concern a different year. The date of the work is a factual input, not a detail to fill in after choosing a preferred rate.

sections.heading: Establish the industry and actual worker role
paragraphs: The building-service poster separately addresses residential janitor pay by unit or weekly salary, and a residential-janitor overtime exception. A commercial cleaning business cannot apply that treatment simply because its employees clean a building. Determine the actual industry and role.

The miscellaneous poster contains its own extra-pay and credit notes and says no tip credit is available. Do not import a restaurant hospitality credit into another wage order. The posters also flag overtime, uniform maintenance and, where applicable, call-in pay or spread of hours. This guide does not decide whether a particular overtime exemption applies.

sections.heading: Worked example: two otherwise similar weekly budgets
paragraphs: Fictional example: a service company budgets 30 covered hours each week for one employee at a Westchester office and another at an Albany office. Using only the cited general 2026 hourly floors, the base figures are 30 × $17 = $510 and 30 × $16 = $480. The regional difference is $30 per week.

Those figures illustrate the location question; they are not complete payroll quotations. The payroll owner next confirms the correct wage order and worker category and examines the applicable extra-pay questions. Employer taxes, insurance, benefits and other costs are separate budget lines.

If someone proposes a lower residential-janitor or tip-credit calculation, the manager asks for the actual legal and factual basis instead of accepting it because it lowers the bid. The example supplies a method for identifying questions, not permission to use a particular exemption.

sections.heading: Keep 2027 information and proposals distinct
paragraphs: As read for the recorded review, the NYDOL overview displays a 2027 table and announces that the standard $17/$16 rates will remain unchanged under an off-ramp. It separately announces a home-care increase and describes a Governor’s proposal to change the off-ramp provisions.

An administrative announcement and proposed legislation are different evidence. Use the dated 2026 posters for 2026 work. Before 2027 payroll, recheck enacted law and current agency guidance rather than treating a proposal as an adopted rule or using this dated review as a permanent rate sheet.

sections.heading: Build one row for each worksite and worker category
bullets: Record the actual worksite, region and payroll period.
Identify the industry wage order and worker role, including any residential-janitor facts.
Attach the dated source and review overtime, uniforms, call-in pay, spread of hours and any claimed credit.
Budget employer taxes, insurance, benefits and operating costs separately.
Assign unresolved category or exemption questions before relying on a lower figure.

practicalOutput: A worksite payroll worksheet showing the region, wage order, worker category, dated rate and unresolved extra-pay questions.
limitations: This covers the named wage-planning issue, not a complete employment, franchise, tax, licensing or local-law review.
Actual entity, worksite, worker, industry and date facts control the inquiry. No worker classification or exemption is approved, and the 2027 announcement/proposal distinction remains explicit.

title: North Carolina business opportunities: check each promise separately
description: Understand why a U.S. trademark registration may answer one definition branch without removing other business-opportunity duties.
learningSummary: A branded offer can also promise help finding customers, a refund or a minimum income. North Carolina’s business-opportunity rules require attention to the actual promises, not just the brand registration. The seller must establish the relevant definition or exemption and then distinguish filing from delivery of information to the buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: An arrangement to examine under the state’s particular business-startup definition; it is not a label the seller can settle by choice.
A statement or promise made to a prospective purchaser.
The stated U.S. trademark or service-mark registration, distinct from a foreign registration or pending application.
A financial protection mechanism whose applicability and requirements must be checked under the relevant provision.

sections.heading: Start with the four kinds of promise
paragraphs: Article 19 describes specified business-starting arrangements connected with vending-machine or similar-device placement, buying products made by the purchaser, income or refund promises, or a sales/marketing programme. Write down what the seller actually undertakes to do under each possible branch.

The federally registered-mark exception is located within the marketing-programme limb of section 66-94(4). It does not erase the other listed representations. A registration in the home country or a pending U.S. application is not a substitute for the stated U.S. registration condition.

sections.heading: A covered offer has filing and updating tasks
paragraphs: For a covered business opportunity, section 66-97 requires filing before advertising or other representations to prospective purchasers in the state. It also requires material-change updates and updates at least annually. Filing therefore needs an owner before the campaign, rather than being treated as paperwork after a sale.

Section 66-94.1 provides a separate responsible-seller exemption with its own conditions and sworn filing. A sworn filing is a formal statement made with the required verification. A company’s good reputation alone does not establish this exemption.

sections.heading: Worked example: a cleaning brand with an income guarantee
paragraphs: Fictional example: a Singapore brand has a registered U.S. service mark and offers cleaning operators customer-account assistance plus an income guarantee. The manager initially assumes the mark removes every business-opportunity question.

The team separates the marketing programme from the guarantee. It records precisely what income is promised, any refund terms and who is responsible. The mark condition may be relevant to one branch, but the guarantee needs its own analysis. Customer-account assistance also does not, by itself, establish the distinct vending-device placement trigger.

Finance examines whether the promises lead to a bond or trust requirement. Sales retains the actual advertisement, script and proposed agreement so the legal review concerns what buyers will really be told. This fact-gathering example does not classify the arrangement or approve a guarantee.

sections.heading: Delivery to the buyer uses a separate clock
paragraphs: Section 66-95 requires covered state disclosure at least 48 hours before the earlier signature or receipt of consideration, meaning money or other value for the commitment. It permits a materially compliant federal FDD as one content route. An FDD is the franchise disclosure document given to a prospective buyer.

Using that document does not shorten an independently applicable federal 14-calendar-day requirement. Keep evidence of the actual version delivered and the earliest signature/payment, and apply each relevant clock. A filing receipt and a buyer-delivery receipt establish different events.

sections.heading: Build a promise-and-date sheet
bullets: Retain the actual U.S. mark registration and rights to license it.
List marketing, device-placement, product-buyback, refund and income promises separately.
Document the chosen classification/exemption and any required filing or sworn statement.
Log first advertising, other representations, document delivery, signature and consideration.
Assign financial statements, guarantee/bond/trust evidence, updates and annual review to named owners.

practicalOutput: A four-promise factsheet linked to separate state filing and buyer-disclosure calendars.
limitations: This covers the stated North Carolina business-opportunity branches, not every franchise, dealer, tax, employment, sector or local requirement.
The guide supplies no transaction-specific permission to offer, sell, open or terminate. A mark exception or responsible-seller exemption must be established on its own actual conditions.

title: North Dakota franchises: plan renewal before registration expires
description: Learn what the April 2026 addendum change does—and why it leaves other registration, disclosure and record duties in place.
learningSummary: An operator may no longer need one state-specific document while the seller still has registration and disclosure duties. North Dakota’s April 2026 addendum notice is that kind of narrow change. The franchisor should update the right checklist item while continuing to track registration effectiveness, renewal, material changes and delivery to buyers.

keyTerms.meaning: An additional document or section attached to the main disclosure package.
An order affecting the offering’s ability to proceed; check its actual legal effect.
Holding fees under specified controls rather than treating them as immediately available cash.
A financial assurance alternative subject to its applicable conditions.
Relief from a stated requirement where authorised; it must not be assumed.
The state-defined arrangement granting a subfranchisor rights, for consideration, to sell or negotiate franchise sales in the franchisor’s name or on its behalf.

sections.heading: First establish the agreement and state connections
paragraphs: Section 51-19-02 covers the stated combination of marketing plan/system, commercial symbol and direct or indirect fee, including area-franchise scope. Required goods or services can matter. Its wholesale-goods exclusion has a reasonable-quantity condition, so purchasing stock is not automatically outside the fee inquiry.

The section also defines state-connected offers/acceptances and distinguishes uninterrupted renewals/extensions within its offer/sale definition. That contract-renewal distinction does not cancel the separate duty to renew registration. Identify the parties, payments, location facts and transaction type before selecting an exemption.

sections.heading: Submission and effectiveness are different events
paragraphs: Section 51-19-03 requires registration or an applicable exemption before a covered offer or sale. Under 51-19-07, filing, entry into the register by the Commissioner—the responsible state official—and the absence of a stop order matter to effectiveness. A submitted application is not itself proof that every condition has been met.

Material changes require prompt written amendment notification; approved amendments take effect on the Commissioner’s date. Any conditional fee escrow/impoundment or surety alternative also depends on the statute and actual order. Keep these conditions with the offering’s cash and date records.

sections.heading: Renewal comes before the expiry-day reminder
paragraphs: The agency directs renewal no later than fifteen business days before registration expires unless the Commissioner waives the period. It describes a twelve-month registration period unless an order or rule says otherwise. Use the effective and expiry dates from the actual registration record.

The agency also says that from April 1, 2026 a state-specific FDD addendum is no longer required. This changes one document task. It does not remove registration, financial review, disclosure or amendment responsibilities.

sections.heading: Worked example: updating last year’s checklist
paragraphs: Fictional example: a Netherlands maintenance network reuses its old North Dakota renewal file. The coordinator sees the April 2026 notice and removes the obsolete addendum assumption through a documented checklist revision, retaining the earlier version so the change can be understood.

The renewal owner still checks the FDD, marked changes, accountant consent, seller forms and advertising not previously filed. Finance examines any financial-assurance condition. The owner records the fifteen-business-day deadline and any actual waiver rather than relying on a reminder sent on expiry day. The narrow change saves the wrong document from being prepared; it does not make the whole renewal unnecessary.

sections.heading: Buyer delivery and preserved rights remain separate
paragraphs: Section 51-19-08(6) has its stated seven-day prospectus/agreement delivery rule before the earlier agreement or consideration, plus a signed receipt and three-year receipt retention. The independently applicable federal 14-calendar-day rule is not shortened by that state text.

Section 51-19-16(7) separately makes purported waiver of compliance with the chapter, rules or orders void. This is the named anti-waiver provision, not a complete answer about every termination, renewal or industry protection. The agency’s broad count of registration states is also not used here as a national classification.

sections.heading: Prepare the current filing and delivery record
bullets: Keep actual registration effectiveness, register entry, expiry and order information.
Calculate the renewal deadline and retain any written waiver.
Document the addendum-checklist change without deleting the history.
Assign financial-assurance and material-change tasks; retain each document version.
Log buyer delivery, earliest commitment, signed receipt and required retention.

practicalOutput: A revised renewal checklist tied to actual registration dates, a separate buyer-delivery record and a traceable April 2026 template revision.
limitations: This covers the stated franchise definition, process and document issues, not corporate tax, employment, permits or address-dependent operating duties.
Actual parties, offer locations, exemptions and orders require review. The addendum change is not general deregulation, and the named anti-waiver rule is not a complete relationship-law opinion.

title: Ohio business opportunities: read what the exemption leaves in place
description: Understand why federal-compliant disclosure may remove many state duties while leaving security and buyback questions open.
learningSummary: Giving a prospective operator a franchise disclosure document does not answer every Ohio question. The stated FTC-compliance exemption preserves particular provisions about security and buyback promises. The seller must also establish whether the actual transaction fits that exemption or another state exception before relying on it.

keyTerms.meaning: Federal Trade Commission, the U.S. agency responsible for the federal franchise rule discussed here.
A promise to buy property back under stated circumstances.
The representation that payment or a debt document has the stated protection; examine the actual promise and supporting arrangement.
For the reviewed Ohio rule, a count excluding Sunday and legal holidays—not automatically a Monday–Friday count.

sections.heading: An exemption can preserve named duties
paragraphs: Section 1334.13 exempts materially FTC-compliant transactions from most of Ohio’s Business Opportunity Plans chapter. Its opening wording preserves sections 1334.03(H) and 1334.04. Those provisions address representations that a payment or note is secured, or that a buyback arrangement exists, and related bond or trust requirements.

The practical question is therefore not just “Did we provide an FDD?” An FDD is information for a prospective franchise buyer. The company must retain evidence of the relevant federal compliance and examine any preserved Ohio provision triggered by the actual promises.

sections.heading: Start with Ohio’s own definitions and proof requirements
paragraphs: Section 1334.01 defines the state arrangement using supplied goods or services, payment conditions and specified representations. Its payment analysis is separate from the federal minimum-payment exemption. Do not substitute a federal payment test for the state definition.

Section 1334.12 contains other exceptions. In cases under sections 1334.08 or 1334.09, section 1334.14 places proof of an exemption or exception on the person claiming it. A written explanation linked to the facts is therefore more useful than an unexplained box marked exempt.

sections.heading: Worked example: equipment advertised as protecting the investment
paragraphs: Fictional example: a European technical-services brand gives an Ohio prospect an FDD. Its salesperson also says the startup payment is “fully secured” because the brand will buy back equipment if the unit closes. Those words create a separate question from whether the federal disclosure process was completed.

The finance manager keeps the precise statement, identifies who made it and obtains the actual buyback agreement. The reviewer checks the surviving Ohio security/buyback provisions and any bond or trust requirement, including the required amount if applicable. A verbal reassurance or an accounting entry is not a substitute for analysing the promised protection.

The example does not establish that this offer is covered or that a particular financial arrangement satisfies the law. It shows why marketing language and the finance documents need to be reviewed together.

sections.heading: The nonexempt route has its own buyer protections
paragraphs: For a covered plan without an established exemption, the chapter has disclosure, claim-substantiation, contract and cancellation provisions. The basic disclosure period is ten business days before agreement. Ohio’s reviewed definition excludes Sunday and legal holidays; a standard Monday–Friday calculator may produce the wrong count.

Cancellation under section 1334.05 is a separate conditional process, not a universal right for every franchise buyer to cancel. Determine the applicable route and conditions before describing any cancellation right or preparing the contract notice. Independently applicable federal requirements remain separate.

sections.heading: Assemble the exemption and promise file
bullets: List every security, refund and buyback statement and retain the exact wording.
Attach the relevant FTC-compliance evidence and precise Ohio exemption or exception.
Assign finance to the bond/trust question and any required amount or supporting document.
For a covered nonexempt plan, build the correct business-day calendar and contract/cancellation record.
Review equipment-dealer and other industry relationship laws separately.

practicalOutput: A documented exemption decision plus a finance file connecting each security or buyback promise to its actual supporting arrangement.
limitations: The page covers the stated Ohio branches, not all franchise, dealer, tax, employment, sector or local duties.
No particular exemption, bond/trust arrangement, cancellation or planned sale is approved. The surviving provisions must be tested even when the relevant exemption otherwise applies.

title: Oklahoma offers: separate the exemption, registration and advertising questions
description: Learn how document delivery, state connections and the chosen filing route fit together without treating an FDD as complete permission.
learningSummary: A business recruiting an Oklahoma operator first needs a reasoned decision about the state route. One exemption depends on timely delivery of a stated document, while the registration route has its own effectiveness rules. Neither route turns filing into approval or resolves the advertising-rule information that remains unavailable.

keyTerms.meaning: A provision removing an arrangement from a defined category when its conditions are met.
A provision relieving specified duties after its conditions are established.
Money or other value given in connection with the commitment.
A registration that has reached the required legal stage; a submission alone may not establish it.

sections.heading: Identify exactly what the disclosure exemption removes
paragraphs: The Oklahoma Business Opportunity Sales Act prohibits covered offers or sales without registration or an exemption. Section 803(6) provides a disclosure-based exemption for specified business opportunities or franchises when the stated document is delivered 14 calendar days before the earlier binding agreement or consideration.

The provision exempts sections 806–811 rather than the whole Act. Record the exact paragraph being used, which duties it removes and what remains. Merely preparing a document does not establish delivery, recipient or timing.

sections.heading: Use the state definition and actual locations
paragraphs: Section 802 contains Oklahoma definitions of business opportunity, franchise and marketing plan. Promises about finding accounts and providing training can be relevant. A separate registered-mark/net-worth exclusion has further conditions; a registered mark alone does not establish it.

Section 805 places the burden of proving an exemption, exclusion or exception on its claimant. Section 818 separately examines the relevant offer origin and receipt, acceptance, domicile and operating-location facts. Domicile concerns the legally relevant home connection, rather than just where a salesperson happens to be travelling. An internet campaign needs its actual communications analysed; this guide supplies no blanket rule for discovery calls.

sections.heading: Worked example: a cross-border industrial-services campaign
paragraphs: Fictional example: a Dutch brand prepares an FDD and expects Oklahoma responses for an operation nearby. The expansion manager lists the selling entity, where offers originate and arrive, how acceptance occurs, the relevant domicile and where the operator will work.

The finance manager separately lists proposed agreements, deposits and other early commitments. If the company relies on section 803(6), the file must establish the specified document’s actual delivery and the 14-calendar-day period before the earlier covered event. If that route is not established, the team obtains a decision on registration or another applicable provision instead of assuming that the FDD alone finishes the task.
