bullets: Record state coverage, the actual action and the relevant agreement dates.
Keep the territory/customer map and any competitive appointment proposal.
Attach cause evidence, comparable standards, repeated-breach history and correction records.
Separate goodwill from item source, eligibility, condition and offsets.
Assign settlement/release, insolvency and remedy questions independently.

practicalOutput: A relationship-action file with distinct territory, cause/cure and termination-versus-expiry compensation records.
limitations: This does not provide a full damages, limitation-period, insolvency or litigation analysis; section 190 remedies are not a forecast of an award.
Actual agreements, statutory conditions and evidence require review. No exit or remedy is approved, and federal, industry, employment, tax and local duties remain separate.

title: West Virginia equipment dealers: map inventory, repairs and the exit process
description: Learn why the dealer definition and item records matter before applying the six-month termination rule or estimating repurchase.
learningSummary: A supplier may appoint a partner to sell equipment and repair it, while also licensing a service brand. West Virginia’s reviewed equipment-dealer law has its own coverage conditions and exit duties. Define the equipment and operating roles first, then treat notice, return and payment as separate tasks.

keyTerms.meaning: The statute’s conditions for the covered seller and its activities, rather than anyone using the commercial title dealer.
Giving the written notice using the prescribed method, not just drafting or informally sending a message.
The relevant statutory pricing evidence to retain; it is not automatically the retail price or accounting balance.
Buying back property that qualifies under the applicable statutory conditions.

sections.heading: The title does not limit the inquiry to farm machines
paragraphs: The Farm Equipment Dealer Contract Act includes specified retail sellers of construction, industrial and outdoor power equipment, with inventory and repair-service conditions. Those conditions are part of coverage, not optional background facts.

The supplier and operator should record what is sold at retail, which inventory obligations exist and who provides repairs. A brand licence or service contract alone does not establish that the Act applies. Conversely, a business should not ignore the Act simply because its equipment is industrial rather than agricultural.

sections.heading: Notice is a procedure, not only a period
paragraphs: Section 47-11F-3 generally requires six months’ termination notice, prescribed written service and stated contents. Listed exceptions and a mutual-consent route need separate examination. Keep the reason, method, contents and effective date together.

Do not casually replace six months with an assumed number of days or treat an informal message as proof of prescribed service. Nor does the existence of a contract clause settle whether the relevant statutory branch and exception have been followed. This guide does not choose a termination route for any actual relationship.

sections.heading: Worked example: equipment sales alongside a maintenance service
paragraphs: Fictional example: a European maintenance brand appoints a West Virginia partner to sell machines and provide repairs. The commercial plan describes the whole arrangement as a service partnership, but the operator also has equipment inventory commitments.

The operations manager separates retail sales, repair services and branded customer work. The reviewer uses those facts to test dealer coverage. Finance builds item records with purchase source, age, condition, ownership and pricing evidence before a possible exit.

If the supplier later proposes termination, the secretary identifies the actual event and examines the notice method, contents, date and any claimed exception or mutual-consent route. The contract and the operational records are read together. The example illustrates preparation; it does not establish that either party qualifies or that termination is lawful.

sections.heading: Inventory value and payment are different questions
paragraphs: Sections 4–5 govern conditional inventory repurchase, including valuation, timing and exclusions. A gross stock balance cannot show what qualifies, whether an item is excluded or how its value must be measured.

Track the termination date, physical return and payment separately. Finance should retain the relevant current-net-price evidence and any return information, then identify the responsible payer and unresolved warranty issues. A company can budget possible exposure while leaving disputed eligibility or amounts open; the budget itself is not a legal entitlement.

sections.heading: Keep an inventory-and-service decision file
bullets: Describe retail sales, repair services, products and inventory commitments for the definition test.
Retain the agreement and supporting operational records.
Log the notice reason, prescribed method, contents, effective date and claimed exception.
Keep item-level age, condition, source, title, pricing and exclusion evidence.
Assign repurchase return/payment responsibilities and remaining warranty questions separately.

practicalOutput: A product-and-service coverage file connected to the actual notice procedure and an itemised return, valuation and payment record.
limitations: This is the stated equipment-dealer branch, not a general rule for every West Virginia franchise or a complete state-law survey.

Actual definitions, notice exceptions, mutual-consent conditions and repurchase requirements must be applied to the facts. Other franchise, dealer, tax, employment, sector and local duties remain separate.

title: Wisconsin franchise registration: a receipt does not certify the business
description: Understand registration on receipt, the separate buyer-disclosure period and annual or material-event filing tasks.
learningSummary: Wisconsin describes a registration process that does not evaluate the business’s merits. That can make the filing event relatively straightforward, but it does not approve the model or replace the buyer’s disclosure period. The seller should track the franchise system, document version and actual events separately.

keyTerms.meaning: Wisconsin Department of Financial Institutions, the regulator publishing the cited instructions.
A regulator’s evaluation of the offering’s merits; the agency says Wisconsin does not conduct that franchise review.
Franchise Disclosure Document: information for a prospective buyer, not a government certificate of quality.
An important event requiring examination under the applicable amendment rules.
The shared financial-interest concept relevant to the separate dealership-law inquiry, based on actual relationship facts.

sections.heading: Registration and buyer delivery have different starting events
paragraphs: DFI says a franchise must be registered no later than its first Wisconsin franchise sale. Registration is described as effective on receipt, and the agency expressly says Wisconsin is not a franchise merit-review state. A buyer should not treat the receipt as validation of projections, management or the model.

The agency separately requires an FDD 14 calendar days before the earlier signing of a binding franchise or other agreement, or payment. Filing on receipt does not start or replace that buyer-delivery clock. Keep the recipient, document version and actual delivery date.

sections.heading: Each system and each event needs the correct filing record
paragraphs: DFI lists a $400 registration fee and one-year effectiveness, and says each franchise system needs a separate filing. A group should identify whether it is selling different systems instead of assuming one corporate name means one filing.

The agency lists material-event amendments within 30 days, with a $200 fee. An amendment does not restart the registration year. These amounts were checked against the agency FAQ on the recorded review date and should be rechecked before payment. A diary entry for next year’s renewal cannot replace reviewing a material event now.

sections.heading: Worked example: two service systems and a reorganisation
paragraphs: Fictional example: a group sells a facilities-management franchise system and a separate pest-control franchise system. Its secretary identifies the separate filing scope, retains each receipt and connects each buyer-delivery record to the correct FDD and agreement.

Later, the group reorganises its corporate structure. Rather than waiting automatically for annual renewal, the secretary sends the actual change for assessment as a possible material event. If an amendment is required, its timing and fee are recorded without replacing the existing registration-year dates.

The sales manager separately checks that each prospective buyer’s 14-calendar-day period has run before the earlier covered agreement or payment. A same-day registration receipt cannot show that the buyer received the right documents two weeks earlier. The example demonstrates event control, not approval of a particular filing or reorganisation.

sections.heading: The operating relationship has its own legal test
paragraphs: The agency FAQ also points to Wisconsin’s Fair Dealership Law. Chapter 135’s dealership/community-of-interest inquiry is independent of sales registration. A registration receipt or federal franchise-fee analysis does not decide whether that operating law applies.

The separate dealership guide addresses in-state scope, exclusions, good cause, notice/cure and marked inventory. In particular, the nonpayment branch does not turn a ten-day cure notice into an automatic day-11 termination right. Keep relationship changes and exits assigned even where registration is straightforward.

sections.heading: Prepare the filing and delivery calendar
bullets: Identify each franchise system and retain its filing/receipt and annual dates.
Keep the FDD version, recipient and delivery date before agreement/payment.
Review important events for the 30-day amendment task; do not restart the year because an amendment is filed.
Recheck the current fee before payment.
Assign the independent Fair Dealership Law and other operating-law questions.

practicalOutput: A system-by-system registration, buyer-delivery and amendment calendar that never describes receipt as merit approval.
limitations: This covers the stated franchise sales and filing issues, not tax, employment, permits or address-dependent operating requirements.
Actual parties, system scope, offers and exemptions need review. Fair Dealership Law coverage and notice/cure rights require their own facts; no filing or transaction is approved.

title: Wisconsin dealership exits: cause, advance notice and cure are different requirements
description: Understand why nonpayment does not automatically permit day-11 termination and why only specified marked inventory qualifies for repurchase.
learningSummary: A Wisconsin franchise registration receipt answers a sales-filing question. It does not decide whether the ongoing arrangement is a protected dealership or whether the supplier may change or end it. Identify the actual dealership facts first, then separate the justification, advance notice, correction period and inventory consequences.

keyTerms.meaning: The party granting the dealership rights under this chapter.
The grantee of a qualifying dealership situated in Wisconsin; the statutory conditions still need to be established.
The financial-interest relationship concept requiring evidence about the actual business arrangement.
Correcting a stated default within the applicable period.
A court order requiring or preventing conduct, available only under the applicable conditions.

sections.heading: Use the operating-law definition
paragraphs: Chapter 135 can include express or implied, oral or written agreements granting sale/distribution rights or use of a commercial symbol, with a community of interest. A federal fee analysis or Wisconsin registration does not establish that separate test.

Section 135.07 excludes the specified motor-vehicle dealer/distributor/wholesaler acting in that capacity, insurance business and door-to-door marketing of goods or services. Liquor has its own provisions. Record how the business actually sells and operates rather than assuming a trademark either creates protection or establishes an exclusion.

sections.heading: Justification and notice both need evidence
paragraphs: Section 135.03 prohibits covered termination, cancellation, nonrenewal and substantial competitive changes without good cause, placing the burden of establishing cause on the grantor. Calling conduct a default does not establish that cause exists.

Section 135.04 ordinarily requires 90 days’ prior written notice stating all reasons and 60 days to rectify the claimed deficiency. Timely correction voids the notice. Insolvency, assignment for creditors and bankruptcy have stated notice exceptions; examine the actual branch rather than extending the ordinary rule to every event.

sections.heading: For nonpayment, distinguish ten days to fix from the advance notice
paragraphs: The statute supplies written nonpayment-default notice and ten days to remedy from delivery or posting. The cited official civil jury instruction’s comment expressly preserves 90 days’ advance notice for this branch while shortening cure to ten days.

The two clocks answer different questions. One concerns the opportunity to fix the payment problem; the other concerns advance notice of the proposed action. A ten-day demand should therefore not be scheduled as automatic authority to terminate on day 11. The older instruction is used for this specific explanation alongside the current certified statute.

sections.heading: Worked example: unpaid invoices and a nearby replacement
paragraphs: Fictional example: a British grounds-care supplier plans to end a Wisconsin dealer after unpaid invoices and appoint a nearby seller. The manager first tests dealership/community-of-interest coverage and exclusions. The proposed competitive change is recorded as well as the proposed termination.

The team preserves the cause evidence, default wording and delivery/posting record, then separately calendars the applicable advance notice and correction requirements. Finance identifies grantor-marked resale stock separately from service tools. A supplier cannot assume that selecting the shortest apparent deadline completes the other conditions. This example does not decide cause or authorise the action.

sections.heading: Inventory and remedies have their own conditions
paragraphs: Under section 135.045, grantor-initiated termination can trigger, at the dealer’s option, repurchase at fair wholesale market value of qualifying inventory sold by the grantor for resale. The section is confined to merchandise bearing an identifying grantor mark. A computer or service tool does not qualify merely because it helped run the business.
Section 135.06 provides a conditional damages, costs/fees and injunction route. A checklist does not establish injury, an award or a successful court application.

sections.heading: Prepare the action file
bullets: Keep in-state dealership facts, agreement rights, community-of-interest evidence and exclusion analysis.
Identify the actual proposed action and cause evidence.
Retain all reasons, notice delivery/posting, separate clocks and correction records.
Identify grantor-supplied marked resale inventory and valuation evidence.
Assign remedy, arbitration, federal and specialised industry questions separately.

practicalOutput: A dealership-action file separating cause, 90-day advance notice, ordinary/nonpayment cure and qualifying marked-inventory evidence.
limitations: No independent full appellate opinion was reviewed; the older official jury instruction is used only for the specific notice explanation alongside current certified statute.
Arbitration, federal preemption, liquor and complete community-of-interest case law remain outside this guide.
No actual action, remedy or agreement is approved. Federal, sector, employment, tax and local duties remain separate.

title: Wyoming equipment dealers: identify the notice regime before ending the agreement
description: Learn why general and single-line dealer branches have different notice periods and why inventory has its own review.
learningSummary: An operator can sell machines and parts while also providing local services. Wyoming’s equipment-dealer law concerns defined products and relationships, not every service franchise. Once coverage is established, the relevant dealer category and reason for action determine which notice and correction rules need to be examined.

keyTerms.meaning: The particular statutory dealer category whose conditions must be tested; one branded product alone is not a substitute for that analysis.
Correcting the stated problem under the applicable procedure.
The party in the equipment-supply role defined by the law, rather than any contractor on the project.
A conditional supplier buyback of qualifying property after the relevant event.

sections.heading: Separate the equipment arrangement from customer services
paragraphs: Title 40, Chapter 20 addresses defined equipment dealers and suppliers. Its product scope includes specified industrial, maintenance, utility and grounds-care equipment. Dealer status, single-line status, exclusions and the actual agreement must be checked before using these protections.

Describe machines, parts, repair rights and the customer services separately. Owning equipment or using a brand does not automatically answer the supplier/dealer test. This factual separation also helps the company see which stock and required tools create possible exit exposure.

sections.heading: The two ordinary notice regimes are different
paragraphs: The general sections 115/117 regime ordinarily uses 180 days’ notice with 60 days to cure. The single-line section 116 regime ordinarily uses 90 days with 60 days to cure. First establish the actual branch; do not choose whichever period fits the preferred commercial schedule.

Specified events and performance failures have different conditions. Preserve the reason for action, comparable performance standards, relevant notices and improvement history. These are conditional industry rules, not a general right to end any franchise simply by waiting out a notice period.

sections.heading: Worked example: grounds-care sales plus service contracts
paragraphs: Fictional example: an overseas brand supplies machines, parts and repair know-how to a Wyoming operator that also sells grounds-care services to local customers. The team’s first draft treats the entire relationship as a single service licence.

The operations manager separates equipment dealership rights from the operator’s customer-service contracts. The reviewer tests the actual products, dealer/supplier status, exclusions and any single-line conditions. If the supplier later proposes termination, the file identifies the actual action and reason before selecting the general or single-line notice branch.

Finance has already retained inventory and required-tool records. That allows a later repurchase review without assuming that the supplier must repay every startup cost. Any succession request is recorded with its actual facts rather than being treated as resolved by the termination calendar.
The example illustrates why the agreement and operational evidence need to be read together. It does not decide that the operator is protected, establish a performance default or authorise an exit.

sections.heading: Repurchase does not follow automatically from the notice figure
paragraphs: Sections 120–121 contain repurchase duties and exclusions. Coverage of the relationship does not establish eligibility of every item. Record the property, source, dates, condition, return events and payment questions separately from the cause and notice decision.

The separate Wyoming inventory guide explains the detailed evidence categories. A financial estimate can help management plan, but it should show assumptions and unresolved items instead of treating the accounting stock balance as a guaranteed recovery.

sections.heading: Prepare the branch-and-event record
bullets: Attach product, dealer and supplier definitions and exclusion facts.
Document why the general or single-line branch is relevant.
Record the action, reason, performance standards and any specific exception.
Keep notice, correction and performance-improvement history in date order.
Identify inventory eligibility, returns, payment duties and any succession request for separate review.

practicalOutput: A Wyoming equipment relationship file identifying the actual notice branch and linking it to distinct inventory and succession questions.
limitations: This concerns the defined equipment-dealer branch, not a general Wyoming franchise-exit rule or complete state-law survey.

Actual dealer categories, exclusions, performance conditions and exceptions require review. Other franchise, tax, employment, industry and local duties remain independent, and no termination is approved.

title: Wyoming equipment buybacks: build a ledger before estimating recovery
description: Understand the different price bases, item conditions, return triggers and payment events in a covered dealer exit.
learningSummary: An inventory balance is not a legal buyback amount. Wyoming’s reviewed equipment-dealer provisions use different conditions and price bases for machines, parts, required technology and specialised tools. Finance needs item-level evidence and a separate record of return and receipt before treating an expected amount as cash recovered.

keyTerms.meaning: The statute’s defined equipment-price basis, not automatically book value or retail price.
The separate defined price basis for qualifying repair parts.
Allocating acquisition cost evenly over the stated period, subject to the rule’s actual qualifications.
The required ownership position without the disqualifying claims addressed by the relevant provision.
Reducing sums owed on an account rather than necessarily paying cash to the dealer.

sections.heading: Confirm the relationship and separate the item categories
paragraphs: Chapter 40-20 defines the relevant dealer, supplier, equipment and agreement. Dealer status combines selling/leasing to consumers and repair/service activities with stated exclusions. Mere ownership of a machine is insufficient. Closing a covered location can also raise inventory issues under the agreement definition.

This page concerns repurchase evidence. The separate Wyoming hub addresses good-cause and notice branches. A decision that an item may qualify for buyback does not answer whether the relationship was lawfully ended.

sections.heading: Use the legal price basis, not one percentage for everything
paragraphs: Section 120 distinguishes new eligible equipment, qualifying demonstrators and repair parts. Its ordinary figures include 100% of net equipment cost and 95% of current net parts prices for qualifying items, with separate handling/freight and demonstrator conditions.

Required data-processing hardware/software uses the stated three-year straight-line acquisition-cost approach, with a minimum-specification qualification. Specialised repair tools have a 75% invoice rule. Keep supplier-requirement and actual-cost evidence. An ordinary computer or tool is not automatically eligible because the dealer used it.

sections.heading: Eligibility depends on source, condition and dates
paragraphs: Section 121 addresses damaged packages, parts needing reconditioning, clear title, retained goods, condition, equipment delivered before the stated 36-month window, post-notice orders and goods from other sources. Apply the actual qualifications and exceptions: a broken package does not always mean zero recovery.

The return provision in 121(a)(ix) is tied to the later of effective termination and receipt of required return-policy information, with its stated notice qualification. It is not simply 90 days from any letter. Retain the information, when it arrived and what the notice said before treating a return as late.

sections.heading: Worked example: calculate only the proved eligible items
paragraphs: Fictional example: assume a covered dealer establishes $10,000 of eligible net equipment cost and $2,000 of eligible current net parts prices. The basic calculation is $10,000 × 100% plus $2,000 × 95%, producing $11,900 before separate handling, freight, offsets and other applicable conditions.

The finance owner does not assign the same percentage to technology or tools. Those items get separate rows showing the supplier requirement, specification, acquisition cost and applicable method. Disputed condition, title or age is recorded as an unresolved eligibility question, not silently entered as zero or full recovery.
This is fictional arithmetic. It is not a valuation, approved claim or forecast that the amount will be collected.

sections.heading: Payment runs from another event
paragraphs: Section 120(b) generally requires payment or credit within 90 days after the supplier receives covered property. It permits withholding during failure to satisfy the stated contractual signage-removal obligation. Outstanding sums may produce account credit rather than cash.

Keep supplier receipt, offsets, signage and shared freight evidence with the amount calculation. Sending a request, shipping stock or recording a receivable does not prove supplier receipt or payment.

sections.heading: Prepare the return-and-receipt ledger
bullets: Separate machines, demonstrators, parts, required technology and specialised tools.
Attach invoices, statutory price bases, title, condition, age and current parts evidence.
Retain supplier-required specifications and cost records for technology/tools.
Track effective termination, return-policy information, notice qualification, shipping and actual receipt.
Reconcile debt credits, handling/freight and signage obligations separately from expected cash.
Keep termination/cure, buyback and dispute-remedy questions independently assigned.

practicalOutput: An item-level ledger linking eligibility and statutory valuation to return-policy information, supplier receipt, credits and payment conditions.
limitations: Only Wyoming’s defined equipment-dealer branch is covered; actual item exclusions and qualifications must be applied.
No actual property eligibility, title, return deadline, amount due, tax treatment or recovery is determined.
